name: Week Strip
job: Show week by week how many gates entered the always-run path, and tap a week to read each fix that added one as break, repair, gate, every step cited to a commit.

anatomy.role: A button per week: gates wired as a large count, the week's Monday, shaded by count
Up to three dots under the count: gates wired, a break-to-gate chain, a belief reversal (violet lifted toward text to clear 3:1)
Three numbered steps: what broke, the fix with its commit and date, the gate it wired
A heading naming the picked week and its counts (a live region), any reversed beliefs as a link, then its chains or a plain empty line
One line under the strip: where the counts come from, and that client names are removed

states.name: Latest week
states.note: The default: the newest week is picked.

states.name: The busiest week for chains
states.note: Six fixes each added a gate.

states.name: A quiet week, phone width
states.note: No chain: the readout says so in words.

use_when: A reader should see a hardening record over time: what broke and which check it became.
Every count and chain has a commit a reader could check.
avoid_when: Do not invent a chain; a chain is a commit, and its public words are written from that commit's message.
Not for a single release's checklist: it needs weeks to mean anything.

data.type: [week, monday label, gates, chains[], reversals[], withheld]
data.note: Oldest first, one per ISO week, empty weeks kept; withheld counts chains not shown.
Break and repair are reviewed public words, never the raw commit subject.
The busiest week's gate count; shading scales to it.

access: Each week is a native button with aria-pressed and a label that states its date and counts. The grid is one Tab stop (roving tabindex); arrow keys, Home and End move between weeks, Enter and Space pick.
Only the readout heading is a polite live region, so picking a week announces its date and counts, not every chain.
Counts are printed, so shading and dot colour are never the only signal; the dots are hidden from screen readers because the label says the same.
Nothing animates. Without script the host keeps every chain as a dated list.
gates: `gate_chain_build.py --check` (pre-commit): the table, spec, fragment and template match a rebuild at the pinned hook commit.
`gate_chain_build.py --self-test`: every chain sha exists, no scrub term survives, an unreviewed scope fails.
`gauntlet_log_emit.py --gate`: leak-check, tripwire and wrap-lint on the served page.
